name: Civil unrest
value: Indonesia protest arrests; AJK unrest; Spain
summary: Police held 157 after Yogyakarta protests on 10 Nov; unrest goes on in Pakistani Kashmir; no nationwide deadly unrest
state: Security forces used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets on protesters in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, on 10–11 Nov; police said they detained 157 people and released 154, and HRW called for an inquiry into alleged excessive force (HRW, 12 Nov). In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, unrest continued after the 5 Nov clearance of Rawalakot protest camps, and a Rangers officer died on 8 Nov (Express Tribune, 9 Nov). Housing protests in Madrid and Barcelona on 11 Nov ended in clashes and 18 arrests (The Local). No deadly nationwide unrest was found.
for_you: Travellers to Indonesia, Pakistan-administered Kashmir and Spanish city centres should check FCDO travel advice, which advises avoiding demonstrations. Protests can close roads and disrupt transport at short notice.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests in several countries and deadly unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir; no nationwide deadly unrest

sources.title: Human Rights Watch — Indonesia: Alleged Excessive Force Against Protesters

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
